newsitem.title: USA: KCS ENERGY TO ACCELERATE DRILLING IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: KCS ENERGY TO ACCELERATE DRILLING IN 1998.

text.p: KCS Energy Inc, reporting dropping operating income for the second quarter, said Wednesday it would speed up its drilling program in 1998.
"We intend to accelerate our drilling program and currently plan to drill up to 100 wells in the Manderson Field in 1998," said chief executive James Christmas in a statement.
Christmas added the company's interest in the field "could total more 80 million barrels of oil and 1 trillion cubic-feet of gas."
The company said it has drilled 45 new wells in the Manderson field in Wyoming's Big Horn Basin since 1996, and expected to drill an additional 20 by year end.
KCS Wednesday reported its income from operations dropped to $2.3 million, or $0.08 a share, in the second quarter, compared with $5.5 million, or $0.23 a share, in the 1996 quarter.

The company's quarterly net income dropped to $0.08 a share from $0.21 a share last year, failing Wall Street's expectations. A First Call consensus estimate of six analysts had put KCS's earnings at $0.10 a share for the quarter.
The company attributed the earnings decline to its ending its contract with Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co in January; lower gas and oil prices; and higher financing costs.

KCS's gas production rose 73 percent to 10.9 billion cubic feet in the quarter, from 6.3 billion cubic feet in 1996. The company's oil and liquids production soared 141 percent to 455,000 barrels for the quarter, from 189,000 barrels last year.
The company's stock traded at 22-7/8 Wednesday at around noon, down 5/16.
